r.name: Rob Roy Way
r.description: Long distance walk from Drymen on Loch Lomond to Pitlochry in Highland Perthshire.

r.name: EuroVelo 1 - Atlantic Coast Route - part United Kingdom 1
r.name:fr: EuroVelo 1 - Route du littoral Atlantique - tronçon Royaume-Uni 1

r.name: Birnam Hill Path
r.description: A popular walk requiring hill fitness as the north side path is of mountain hiking grade. The ascent is worthwhile for fabulous views from this commanding peak near the Highland Boundary Fault. To the south lies gentler landscape towards Perth and Strathe

r.name: Loch of the Lowes Path
r.description: Joins Dunkeld with Loch of the Lowes Nature Reserve in a loop. Pleasant woodland walk. Some muddy sections near Fungarth.

r.name: Birnam Riverside Path
r.description: Walk beside the River Tay passing the Birnam Oak. Goes downstream past the water treatment works before turning at the Fisherman's Hut. Returns through Birnam.

r.name: Inver Path
r.description: A short but steep section at the north end may be challenging. Otherwise a great combination of riverside and forest.

r.name: Braan Path
r.description: A stunning walk taking in the Hermitage and Rumbling Bridge waterfalls, along with stunning native woodland near Tomgarrow. Note that shortcutting along the A822 is hazardous and not recommended.

r.name: Corbenic Poetry Path
r.description: The Corbenic Poetry Path meanders through a variety of terrains including open hillside, moorland, ancient native woodlands, hazel coppice, and riverbanks. The path has been designed with a variety of surfaces to be as sensitive as possible to the environ

r.name: Fiddler's Path
r.description: Beautiful riverside path which is mostly hiking grade however there is a short section of steep uneven ground. There are tree roots and trunks to step over.

r.name: Atholl Woods Path
r.description: Includes a short section on road. An open-sided boat shed at Mill Dam provides shelter if required.

r.name: Dunkeld to Aberfeldy Core Path
r.description: Surface suitable for robust bicycles with sturdy wheels on firm but not completely smooth paths. Cycling involves steep gradients and remote, exposed hill sections so fitness, planning and preparation required. Surfaces and gradients easy/moderate for hik

r.name: Inchewan Path
r.description: A lollipop route through the enclosed Inchewan Glen gorge before a loop in open country at at Balhomish and native woodland near Tomgarrow.

r.name: The Duchess and the Bishop's Walk
r.description: A leisurely walk with one small section of steps and gentle inclines. The walk uses the Bishop's Path and Connects with the little know but very picturesque Duchess Bridle Path to reach Dunkeld House Hotel. It then returns via the side of the River Tay.

r.name: The Strathbraan Pilgrims' Path
r.description: Route may be muddy but terrain and gradients are gentle. Some streams are forded - boots required S of River Braan. Path indistinct in sections. Care is needed on road sections, particularly A822.

r.name: Torryvald Route
r.description: Easy woodland walk on good surface (some gradients and a short, flat section with some tree roots). There are frequent marker posts with yellow stripe. The Torryvald Folly is at the highpoint of the path.

r.name: Pine Cone Point Path
r.description: Pleasant out-and-back woodland route on firm path to Pine Cone Point viewpoint. The zig-zag climbing section ascends approximately 100 metres.

r.name: Dunkeld Loch Ordie Butterstone Loop
r.description: Half day cycle on mostly good tracks.

r.name: Duchess Cave and Cave Crag
r.description: Adventurous route to see the Duchess Cave, Waterfall and the famous Cave Crag climbing location. Requires sure-footedness and sturdy footwear. Ideal for fit and adventurous children.

r.name: Loch A Choire Route
r.description: Route up to Loch beneath Ben Vrackie. Mostly hiking grade with some mountain hiking beyond Loch A Choire

r.name: Glen Garr Path
r.description: Mostly good path but boggy in places and liable to fern cover in summer. Gentle gradients.

r.name: Dunkeld Christmas Grotto Walk
r.description: Dunkeld Christmas Eve Grotto Walk visits the cave. There are sections of the route that are on narrow uneven paths (mountain hiking). These sections may be bypassed. Most of the route is hiking.

r.name: Civil Engineering Walk
r.description: A route that has several transport engineering points of interest involving historic hydro, road and rail infrastructure yet also has beautiful scenery. Grade is hiking but with short sections with uneven pathways.

r.name: Rocking Stone Path
r.description: Narrow, uneven, cambered paths with steep drops in places. Views from Polney Crag and the Rocking Stone - a glacial artefact.

r.name: Deuchary Hill from Dunkeld
r.description: The final ascent is steep demanding mountain hiking but most of this route is tracks with no extreme inclines.

r.name: Birnam Hill and The River Tay
r.description: An adventurous route over Birnam Hill, through where the buffalo roamed and back along the River Tay

r.name: Castle Dow Hill Fort
r.description: Good tracks but a stiff climb. Take care not to miss the junction that takes you to the fort. Great views of Strathtay and the north from the fort.

r.name: Dalguise to Dunkeld
r.description: Forestry trails with gradual inclines.

r.name: Dunkeld Dull Strathtay Loop
r.description: From Dunkeld (under the A9 via the underpass) to Dull via Strathbraan and Aberfeldy. Past Aberfeldy, a short detour to Dull makes an interesting stop off. Return but stay north of the Tay and head to Strathtay. Take the Dalguise road and back to Dunkeld.

r.name: Station to the Hermitage
r.description: Arriving by train to Dunkeld and Birnam, a visit to the Hermitage is highly recommended. Please use this route avoiding the A9 (which is unsuitable for pedestrians). Say hello to Niel Gow's statue and pass through his birthplace, Inver.

r.name: Cally Loch and Hatton Circular
r.description: Uses old tracks, muddy in places and with the occasional fallen tree to cross.

r.name: River Tay Way
r.description: This is a newly proposed route.

r.name: River Tay Way Cycle Route
r.description: Combining portions of NCN 7 and 77 to provide a route between Kenmore and Dundee, roughly following the course of the River Tay

r.name: Hermitage, Rumbling Bridge and Inchewan Burn
r.description: Walk that combines parts of the Braan Path and the Inchewan Path to make a loop form Dunkeld

r.name: Duchess Anne to Kings Seat
r.description: Directions to King's Seat Pictish Hill Fort from Dunkeld Community Archive. The final part of this walk is in steep terrain and is for experienced hikers only. If in doubt, employ a guide.

r.name: Craigower Viewpoint
r.description: A challenging climb followed by a gradual descent makes this ideal for a headtorch night walk. Refreshments at the Golf Club afterwards

r.name: Buffalo Hut
r.description: Pleasant walk with fine views south towards lowland Perthshire at this vantage point at the threshold of Highland Perthshire.

r.name: Diversion for Cathedral Path Repairs December 05
r.description: Alternative route whilst path repairs scheduled for the 8-10 December 2025 are underway. The voids the muddy field.

r.name: Dunkeld to Scone
r.description: A sorter, more direct route than River Tay Trail. Boots required and ability to read a map.

r.name: Butterstone Dunkeld Circular
r.description: Good tracks and quiet roads

r.name: Dunkeld to Corbenic Poetry Path
r.description: Mixture of road and compacted track. Not suitable for road racing bicycles. Leisure route.
